html:
The Da'naxda'xw and Awaetlala are two Kwakwaka'wakw groups of the British Columbia coast, now one First Nation. Their home is Knight Inlet, a long fjord that cuts into the Coast Mountains.

At the head of the inlet each spring, people gathered to net eulachon, a small oily fish rendered into grease that was traded along the coast and inland. Like other Kwakwaka'wakw they held winter ceremonies and the potlatch, which Canada banned from 1885 to 1951. Their language, Kwak'wala, is one of the Wakashan languages. Neighbours to the north include the Gwa'sala and 'Nakwaxda'xw.
